q: took out twelve goodly vestments

q: was never lacking in battle with the Achaeans

s: Hector is guardian of Ilius

s: Hector has body his body
q: therefore I am now come to the ships of the Achaeans to ransom his body from you with a great ransom.

s: Hector remains undecayed not wasted (twelve days)
q: he is still just lying at the tents by the ship of Achilles, and though it is now twelve days that he has lain there, his flesh is not wasted nor have the worms eaten him although they feed on warriors.

s: Priam has sons fifty sons (nineteen by one mother and the others by women of his household)

s: Peleus is a father of Achilles (old and growing old)

s: Peleus rules Myrmidons (with prosperity and wealth)

s: Thetis is mother of Achilles (daughter of the old man of the sea)

q: At daybreak Achilles drags him cruelly round the sepulchre of his dear comrade

s: Achaeans are at war with Trojans (in the Trojan War)
q: when the Achaeans came here

s: Achaeans reaches the trench and the wall (before the ships)
q: When they reached the trench and the wall that was before the ships

s: gods are a gods (not subject to mortal care)
q: The immortals know no care, yet the lot they spin for man is full of sorrow

s: gods protect Hector's body (because Hector was dear to them)
q: Such care have the blessed gods taken of your brave son, for he was dear to them beyond all measure.”

s: Hector's body is in Achilles' tent (after Hector's death)
q: he is still just lying at the tents by the ship of Achilles

s: Hector's body is preserved by gods (fresh and unwasted after twelve days)

s: mourning is shared by Achilles (for Peleus and Patroclus)
q: and Achilles now for his father and now for Patroclus, till the house was filled with their lamentation.

s: fortune and suffering are distributed by Jove (as good and evil gifts)
q: He for whom Jove the lord of thunder mixes the gifts he sends, will meet now with good and now with evil fortune

s: Priam travels in Priam's chariot (on the journey to Achilles)
q: The old man made haste to mount his chariot, and drove out through the inner gateway and under the echoing gatehouse of the outer court.

s: Priam seeks the ransom of Hector (to recover Hector's body)
q: therefore I am now come to the ships of the Achaeans to ransom his body from you with a great ransom.

s: Jove is a lord of counsel

q: Then the son of Peleus sprang

q: Then King Priam spoke to them saying

s: Hector is a son (of Priam)

s: Hector is a glory (of Troy and its people)

s: Hector protects Troy (as its saviour and guardian)
q: for you who watched over it are no more—you who were its saviour, the guardian of our wives and children.

q: “Husband,” she cried, “you have died young, and leave me in your house a widow

s: Hector is child of Hecuba (dearest child)
q: “Hector,” she cried, “dearest to me of all my children.

s: Hector is subject of the Trojan lament for Hector (by the women and people of Troy)
q: they laid it upon a bed and seated minstrels round it to lead the dirge, whereon the women joined in the sad music of their lament.

s: Achilles has comrade Patroclus (deceased)
q: with him went his two squires Automedon and Alcimus who were closer to him than any others of his comrades now that Patroclus was no more.

s: Hector receives Hector's funeral rites (after his death)
q: Thus, then, did they celebrate the funeral of Hector tamer of horses.

s: Andromache is wife of Hector
q: “Husband,” she cried, “you have died young, and leave me in your house a widow

q: Foremost among them all Andromache led their wailing as she clasped the head of mighty Hector in her embrace.

s: Hecuba is parent of Hector (mother)
q: “Hector,” she cried, “dearest to me of all my children.

s: Helen is wife of Alexandrus (who brought her to Troy)
q: for I am wife to Alexandrus who brought me hither to Troy

s: Helen is related to Hector (sister-in-law)
q: “Hector,” said she, “dearest of all my brothers-in-law—for I am wife to Alexandrus who brought me hither to Troy

s: Helen leads the Trojan lament for Hector (third among the mourners)
q: then Helen for a third time took up the strain of lamentation.

s: Trojans inhabit Troy (as its people)
q: “Come hither Trojans, men and women, and look on Hector; if ever you rejoiced to see him coming from battle when he was alive, look now on him that was the glory of our city and all our people.”

s: Trojans mourn Hector (at his return to the city)
q: At this there was not man nor woman left in the city, so great a sorrow had possessed them.

s: Achilles has squire Automedon (close companion)
q: with him went his two squires Automedon and Alcimus who were closer to him than any others of his comrades now that Patroclus was no more.

s: Trojans build burial mound (over Hector’s ashes)
q: Then they built a barrow hurriedly over it keeping guard on every side lest the Achaeans should attack them before they had finished.
